options.text: A customs area for flights arriving from outside the region, where visitors report
The control tower frequency
Where to report to the ATS reporting office
The holding point for runway C

explanation: The black C on yellow shows the location of the ATS reporting office, where visiting pilots report.

question: Orange and white striped markers are used to show:

options.text: Taxiway centrelines
Runway thresholds
Helicopter landing areas and the edges of the parking stands
The boundary of the manoeuvring area where it is not clearly defined

explanation: Orange and white striped markers indicate the manoeuvring area boundary where it is not clearly defined, and the limits of unusable areas.

question: A marshaller bends extended arms at the elbows and moves the wands up and down from chest height to head. Meaning?

options.text: Move straight ahead
Stop
Slow down
Turn left

explanation: Bent arms with wands moving up and down from chest to head means move ahead (straight ahead).

question: A marshaller extends the right arm at 90° to the body and makes a come-ahead signal with the left hand. The pilot should:

options.text: Turn right
Slow down
Turn left
Stop

explanation: With the right arm extended, the come-ahead signal by the left hand means turn left (from the pilot's point of view); the rate of motion indicates the rate of turn.

question: A marshaller extends the left arm at 90° to the body and makes a come-ahead signal with the right hand. The pilot should:

options.text: Move straight ahead
Turn right
Hold position
Turn left

explanation: Left arm extended with right-hand come-ahead means turn right from the pilot's point of view.

question: A marshaller fully extends both arms at 90° to the sides and slowly moves them above the head until the wands cross. Meaning?

options.text: Cut engines
Emergency stop
Chocks inserted
Normal stop

explanation: Slowly raising extended arms until the wands cross is the normal stop; abruptly crossing wands above the head is the emergency stop.

question: A marshaller abruptly extends arms and wands to the top of the head, crossing the wands. Meaning?

options.text: Normal stop
Chocks inserted
Hold position
Emergency stop

explanation: The abrupt movement to crossed wands above the head is the emergency stop.

question: A marshaller raises a hand just above shoulder height with open palm, then closes the hand into a fist. Meaning?

options.text: Chocks removed
Cut engines
Set brakes
Release brakes

explanation: Open palm closing into a fist means set brakes; a fist opening into an open palm means release brakes. The marshaller waits for the crew's thumbs up.

question: With arms and wands fully extended above the head, a marshaller moves the wands inward in a jabbing motion until they touch. Meaning?

options.text: Chocks inserted
Emergency stop
Chocks removed
Connect ground power

explanation: Wands moving inward to touch means chocks inserted; moving outward means chocks removed.

question: A marshaller raises the right arm with the wand up and makes a circular motion, while the left arm points to an engine. Meaning?

options.text: Fire in that engine
Start that engine
Cut that engine
Slow down that engine

explanation: The circular motion with the other arm pointing at an engine means start engine(s).

question: A marshaller draws the wand across the throat in a slicing motion. Meaning?

options.text: Disconnect power
Fire
Cut engines
Stop

explanation: The slicing motion across the throat means cut engines.

question: A marshaller moves extended arms downwards in a patting gesture, wands moving up and down between waist and knees. Meaning?

options.text: Move ahead
Slow down
Hold position
Stop

explanation: The patting gesture means slow down.

question: A marshaller fully extends arms and wands downwards at a 45° angle to the sides. Meaning?

options.text: Hold position / stand by
Move back
Slow down
Normal stop

explanation: Arms held down at 45° means hold position / stand by until clear for the next manoeuvre.

question: A marshaller moves the right-hand wand in a fanning motion from shoulder to knee while pointing at an area with the left wand. Meaning?

options.text: Start that engine
Slow down the engine on that side
Move towards the area indicated
Fire in the area indicated

explanation: The fanning motion with the other wand pointing indicates fire in that area.

question: How does a marshaller dispatch an aircraft?

options.text: By waving both wands above the head
With a standard salute, keeping eye contact until the aircraft starts to taxi
By a thumbs up from both hands
By pointing both wands towards the taxiway and then raising them above the head

explanation: A standard salute with the right hand or wand dispatches the aircraft; eye contact is kept until the aircraft has begun to taxi.

question: A person at the wing tip raises the right hand above head level with the wand pointing up and moves the left wand pointing down toward the body. This tells the pilot that:

options.text: The aircraft must stop
The engines may be started
Movement on or off the stand is unobstructed
The wing is too close to an obstacle on that side

explanation: This wingwalker/guide signal indicates that the aircraft's movement on or off the parking position is unobstructed.

question: A marshaller raises fully extended arms straight above the head with wands pointing up. Meaning?

options.text: Emergency stop
Proceed to the next marshaller
Chocks removed
Identify gate

explanation: Both arms fully extended above the head with wands pointing up means identify gate.

question: A pilot raises an arm and hand with fingers extended horizontally in front of the face, then clenches the fist. This tells the ground crew:

options.text: Brakes engaged
Brakes released
Insert chocks
Ready to start engine

explanation: Fingers extended then fist clenched means brakes engaged; fist then fingers extended means brakes released.

question: A pilot extends arms with palms facing outwards and moves the hands inwards to cross in front of the face. This means:

options.text: Insert chocks
Brakes engaged
Cut engines
Remove chocks

explanation: Hands moving inwards to cross in front of the face means insert chocks; hands crossed then moved outwards means remove chocks.

question: A pilot raises three fingers on one hand to the ground crew. On a four-engine aeroplane this means ready to start which engine?

options.text: No. 3, the port inner engine
No. 3, counted from the right wing tip
No. 3, the starboard outer engine
No. 3, the starboard inner engine

explanation: Engines are numbered from the port outer (No. 1), port inner (No. 2), starboard inner (No. 3) to starboard outer (No. 4).
